summary:
ACCEPTABLE to commit. Nothing in this round's seven findings is a disclosure leak or a correctness hole, and I re-verified the load-bearing parts of the feature myself rather than taking the challengers' word for them.

What I confirmed on the code. (1) The ML hunk does what D18 needs. `build_entries` has exactly one non-test caller, `enumerate_entries` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:1739), and it is handed `all_entries_with_pos` — the final, fully-deduped entry list; `build_entries` then only maps over `raw` (the `map` at :935-964 is 1:1, nothing is dropped) and the wire `entries'` is again a 1:1 map (:1800-1825). So `own_uks = Bytehashtab.make_set (map #4 raw)` (:804) is exactly the key set Python turns into `AgentTask.theory_keys` (semantic_interpretation.py:475). `available` (:809) is populated only from the post-filter `wanted_uks` (:822) and `sem_of` (:848-851) is its only reader, so `tmpl_sem` (:886) and `loc_sem` (:887) vanish for this run's own entities and nothing else in the hint changes. A locale of a parent theory is never in `raw` (theory_structure.ML:92-105 subtracts every parent's locale space), so its hint is byte-identical to before. `Bytehashtab` keys are `Word8Vector.vector` (hash_table.ML:340-343) and `make_set` uses `update`, not `update_new` (:237-239), so duplicates and an empty `raw` are both safe. (2) The `_judge` guard is necessary and pinned: `except FatalAgentError: raise` (semantic_interpretation.py:1605-1607) is the one arm of `_run_agent` that does not call `_stop_if_cancelled`, and I ran the mutation myself — with `_judge`'s guard removed, `test_a_cancellation_laundered_into_a_fatal_error_still_writes_nothing` fails and the earlier laundering test still passes, which is exactly the split the two tests claim. (3) The suite: 407 passed, the same 16 pre-existing failures. The SCOPE says 405; the extra two are the two tests in `archive/tests/test_prefilter_regression_phase2.py`, an untracked file belonging to another agent, not to this feature.

The exhaustive disclosure audit (question b) is in `disclosure_paths`: twenty channels, nineteen of them either closed by `own_uks`/`hidden_keys` or structurally unable to carry stored English, and one — the CLI built-ins the interpretation session is allowed — deliberately left open and recorded rather than closed.

Four minor repairs should land in the same commit; none needs another review round, and none touches the gate's correctness. (a) `_collapse_provenance` (semantic_interpretation.py:756) requires BOTH the head line and the `Locale "…":` line before it collapses a sibling, so D18 — which removes the locale line for a locale declared in the theory being interpreted — silently killed the collapse for precisely the case D18 exists for. Dropping the `locale is not None` conjunct restores it, provably without changing a byte when the locale line is present. (b) The round-two rearrangement of `_try_resolve_syntax_token` is not behaviour-preserving: the hidden branch now falls through into `_append_definition`, which the applied round-one ruling explicitly forbade changing, and the rearrangement also left a doubled `uk in hidden_keys` test with a dead `sem = None`. (c) The D18 rule in ML rides on a three-binding argument forty-five lines from the point where the stored text is actually fetched; one extra disjunct in `sem_of` states it where it happens and cannot change behaviour. (d) Two sentences of §15.8 do not describe the code.

I downgraded the finding filed as "major" and rejected one outright. The "payload blow-up" claim is measured against a hypothetical, not against the previous code: my probe over the production `InterpretationTask.format_entries` renders twenty Tarski-style siblings at 10498 chars BEFORE D18 (locale line present, collapse firing) and 8219 chars after — D18 made the payload 22 % smaller, not bigger. The repair takes it to 4761. The CLI-built-ins finding names no defect and its proposed tightening would disable the very capability D18 depends on (the agent must read the theory source), so it is recorded in the disclosure list, not actioned.

rulings.title: Dropping the `Locale "…":` line silently disables the sibling provenance collapse, so every sibling repeats the full head line
rulings.rationale: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, SEVERITY REJECTED AS INFLATED. The mechanism is real and I reproduced it with the production classes: semantic_interpretation.py:756 reads `if head is not None and locale is not None and (head, locale) == prev:`, so a hint with no `Locale "…":` line can never collapse; Tools/semantic_store.ML:804-808 removes that line for every locale declared in the theory being interpreted, which is exactly the theory-declares-and-interprets case D18 was introduced for. The head line — `Generated by a locale interpretation (…): instance of locale "X", qualifier "q", instantiating …` — is therefore re-emitted verbatim per sibling in the batch prompt, the retry prompt and the answer tool's reply (semantic_interpretation.py:770-773, :810, :950). What I reject is the claim that this is 'exactly the payload blow-up the collapse was written to prevent'. The challenger's evidence (799 vs 1004 chars) compares one hint with the locale line against the same hint without it, holding everything else equal; that is not the before/after comparison. My probe over the real `InterpretationTask.format_entries`, twenty Tarski-shaped siblings: pre-D18 (locale line present, collapse firing) 10498 chars; post-D18 as shipped 8219 chars. D18 made the payload 22 % SMALLER, because it also removed the ~1 KB `Locale "…":` text and the `Template meaning:` line. So there is no regression against the previous code and no MCP-cap risk that did not exist before — hence minor, not major. The defect that remains is genuine and worth the one-token repair: a mechanism this change silently disabled, and the repair measures 8219 -> 4761 chars (-42 %) while leaving the with-locale case byte-identical (10498 == 10498, verified). No test pins `_collapse_provenance` today (grep of archive/tests finds no reference), so nothing catches this.
rulings.fix: At semantic_interpretation.py:756 drop the middle conjunct: `if head is not None and (head, locale) == prev:`. With `locale is None` on both entries the pair still matches, the comprehension `[l for l in src if l != locale]` drops nothing (every string is != None), and the head is replaced by the back-reference — verified by probe. When the locale line IS present the output is byte-for-byte what it is today. Keying on the head alone is also the more honest shape: the head names the locale, the qualifier and the whole instantiation, so it IS the identity of the interpretation, and the locale-description line is a consequence of it. Update the docstring at :744-752, which currently says the head line 'AND its Locale "...": description line are both byte-identical to prev'. Optional but cheap: a test rendering three siblings whose hints carry no `Locale "…":` line and asserting entries 2 and 3 read `_HINT_SAME_LOCALE`.

rulings.title: The notation-fallback rearrangement is not behaviour-preserving: the hidden branch now reaches `_append_definition`, and it leaves a doubled predicate with a dead `sem = None`
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED by my own probe, twice over. Round one shipped the hidden branch as an early `return` — ai-artifacts/review_integration/working_tree.diff:271-276, hunk `@@ -1711,6 +1707,12 @@`, `if uk in hidden_keys: return (…)` — and the ruling that ordered the rearrangement closed with the sentence 'Do not change which branches reach `_append_definition`', adding that if that is ever re-opened it must move ALL refusal sites together. The shipped code (semantics.py:1715-1727) replaced the return with an assignment that falls through to `if show_defs:` at :1724. My probe with `_append_definition` stubbed: `_try_resolve_syntax_token(conn, '\\<sqsubseteq>', None, True, show_defs=True, log, frozenset({HID}))` returns the refusal followed by 'Definition:\ndefinition T.b where ...' and reports `append called: 1`; with show_defs=False, `append called: 0`. Meanwhile the tool's other two refusals (:1784-1785 and :1797-1798) still `return refused(typed)` before ever reaching `_append_definition`, so two refusals of one tool now disagree — the exact split the ruling forbade opening at one site. This is NOT a D18 leak: the same probe records 0 `Semantic_DB.query` calls on the hidden branch, and `_append_definition` -> `_get_definition_source` (:1663-1676) returns Isabelle command source, which D18 explicitly tells the agent to read. Hence minor, not major. SCOPE's round-two item 5 ('behaviour identical') is wrong about the shipped code. The second half of the finding is also confirmed: :1714 `sem = None if uk in hidden_keys else Semantic_DB.query(...)` immediately followed by :1715 `if uk in hidden_keys:` evaluates one predicate twice and binds a `sem` the taken branch never reads.
rulings.fix: Restore the prescribed shape, which removes both problems in one edit: make the hidden arm `return prefix + '\n(It belongs to the theory being interpreted; read its definition from the source.)'` and drop the `None if uk in hidden_keys else` guard from :1714, leaving `sem = Semantic_DB.query(uk, with_pretty=with_pretty)` under the single remaining test. If the user ever wants a refusal to carry the defining source, that is a design change and must move all three refusal sites (:1715, :1784-1785, :1797-1798) together — do not settle it by leaving one site diverged.

rulings.title: `_try_resolve_syntax_token` tests `uk in hidden_keys` twice and binds a `sem` that is dead on the hidden branch
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED but SUBSUMED. semantics.py:1714 and :1715 do evaluate the same predicate in consecutive statements, and on the hidden branch `sem` is bound to None and read by nobody (its only readers are the `elif sem is not None` at :1717 and the `else` below it, both unreachable when the key is hidden). This is the weaker half of rest-rearrange-showdefs, which found the same duplication AND the behaviour change the duplication was introduced alongside. One edit closes both; do not treat this as separate work. Ruled fix rather than rejected because the observation is correct and the repair is the same one already ordered — but the challenger stopped one line short of the real defect, which is what `if show_defs:` at :1724 now does to the hidden branch.
rulings.fix: As in rest-rearrange-showdefs: restore the early `return` for the hidden branch and let `sem = Semantic_DB.query(uk, with_pretty=with_pretty)` stand unguarded below it. One predicate, no dead binding, and the branch that must not reach `_append_definition` no longer does.

rulings.title: D18 in the ML hint is enforced on the probe list, not at the disclosure point (`sem_of`)
rulings.rationale: UPHELD as an elegance ruling, not a correctness one — the shipped code does close the path, and I verified that independently. The project rule is explicit that a shape which makes an invariant impossible to violate beats one that asks people to remember it, and this is that situation. Tools/semantic_store.ML:848-851 is where a stored interpretation is actually fetched and handed to the hint, and its text mentions only `available`: `fun sem_of (SOME uk) = if not (Bytehashtab.defined available uk) then NONE else …`. Read alone, it says 'return the stored text of any key the store has one for', which is false and whose falsehood IS the whole D18 guarantee. The guarantee currently follows from a two-step argument spanning three bindings forty-five lines earlier — `available` is populated only inside the `if null wanted_uks` block from `wanted_uks` (:809-822), and `wanted_uks` had `filter_out (Bytehashtab.defined own_uks)` applied (:808) — with the D18 comment (:802-803) sitting at the far end of that chain. A second populator of `available`, or an optimisation that short-circuits the `available` test, reopens D18 with nothing in `sem_of` to stop it. The repair is one disjunct and one hash lookup per provenance line, and it is provably behaviour-preserving: `available` cannot today contain a key of `own_uks`, so the disjunct can never fire on existing inputs. That means no re-review is needed — the implementer's usual REPL restart plus the two ML tests suffice. This is the lowest-priority of the four repairs.
rulings.fix: In Tools/semantic_store.ML, guard at the disclosure point and demote the list filter to what it honestly is: `fun sem_of (SOME uk) = if Bytehashtab.defined own_uks uk orelse not (Bytehashtab.defined available uk) then NONE else …`, carrying the D18 comment (currently :802-803) down to `sem_of` with it, and leaving a one-line note at :808 saying the `filter_out` exists so the `Semantic_Store.contains` round trip does not ask about keys whose answer would be discarded. Then adjust §15.8 (plan edit 1 below) to say both.

rulings.title: §15.8's new sentence enumerates what the degraded hint keeps and misses the `collapsed` line
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED on the code. ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1478-1480 says the hint 'keeps its head, the template's current proposition and the provenance note only'. Tools/semantic_store.ML:895-897 assembles `cat_lines (map_filter I [SOME head, SOME tmpl_line, tmpl_sem, loc_sem, collapsed, SOME "(Provenance shown as context only …)"])`, and `collapsed` (:889-893, 'Under this instantiation the same proposition also arises from: …') is built from `others` — the entry's further provenances — and never goes through `sem_of`, so it survives the D18 filter untouched whenever an entry carries more than one provenance. The word 'only' therefore makes the sentence false for a real case. Nothing leaks: `collapsed` carries template NAMES, not stored English. This is a plan-describes-the-code defect in a paragraph this round added by hand, which is squarely what question (d) asks about, so it is not a nitpick. It shares a sentence with disclosure-plan-15-8-hint-scope-misstated; one rewrite fixes both.
rulings.fix: Rewrite the sentence as plan edit 1 below — drop the closing enumeration in favour of 'the hint degrades to the shape it already has when the store holds no text for that key', and, if an enumeration is wanted at all, include the `Under this instantiation …` line.

rulings.title: §15.8 says the two hint lines are omitted "for an entity of this theory" — that is a blanket drop, not what the code does
rulings.rationale: UPHELD, with the challenger's framing trimmed. The sentence at plan:1477-1479 is 'the run's own keys are dropped from the lookup (`own_uks`), so for an entity of this theory those two lines are omitted'. The challenger says 'read literally this says the lines are omitted from every hint' — that overstates it: the immediately preceding clause names 'the instantiated locale and its template theorem', which is a nearer and more natural antecedent for 'an entity of this theory', and under that reading the sentence is correct. But the phrase genuinely admits both readings, and the wrong one contradicts the constraint the user pinned this round (the hint's behaviour for other theories must not change), so it is worth the clause. The technical half of the finding is correct and I verified it: `filter_out (Bytehashtab.defined own_uks)` is applied to `wanted_uks` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:806-808), which is built from `prim_provenance`'s template/locale keys, not to the entries; a fact of this theory that instantiates a locale of a PARENT theory keeps both lines, because `get_locales_with_positions` (theory_structure.ML:92-105) subtracts every parent's locale space so that locale is never in `raw`. The D18 row at plan:102 binds 'them' to 'an entity this run enumerated', which is unambiguous; §15.8 is the one place that is not. Merged with rest-plan-hint-collapsed into a single rewrite.
rulings.fix: Plan edit 1 below: say WHEN a line is dropped rather than for whom, and add the parent-theory sentence explicitly.

rulings.title: OPEN path: the interpretation session runs with the CLI builtins (`Bash`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`) allowed, which no D18 gate covers
rulings.rationale: The facts are right and I checked them: interpretation_driver/__init__.py:118 defaults `cli_tools=True`, semantic_interpretation.py:1848-1856 builds the interpretation driver without passing it (while the judge at :1800-1808 passes `cli_tools=False` explicitly), and claude_code.py:428-429 unions `_CLI_BUILTINS` — Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Bash, Skill, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch and the task tools — into the hook's allow-set. But this names no defect and the repair it proposes would break the feature. D18's instruction to the agent is literally 'read its definition from the source': Read, Grep and Glob are how the agent obeys it, and removing them makes every refusal a dead end. Nothing in any prompt or tool text names the store, its path, or the reading API. And D18's own wording is already accurate about its scope — 'inside an interpretation session NOTHING HANDS the agent a stored interpretation' (plan:102) is a statement about what the pipeline provides, not a claim that the text is unreachable from a process with a filesystem. Rejected as an action item, but the observation is honest and correctly self-labelled, so I have carried it into `disclosure_paths` as the one explicitly OPEN entry rather than dropping it.
rulings.fix: No code change and no plan change. The channel is recorded as PATH 20 in `disclosure_paths` so the D18 guarantee is read for what it is: no tool this session serves returns a stored interpretation of the theory being interpreted. Do not drop `Bash`/`Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` from the interpretation session's allow-set — the agent needs them to read the theory source, which is what D18 tells it to do.

disclosure_paths: PATH 1 — batch prompt / retry prompt / `answer` tool reply, via `Entry.prompt_extra`: the ML locale-interpretation provenance hint's `Template meaning:` and `Locale "…":` lines (Tools/semantic_store.ML:886-888, fed by `sem_of` :848-862, printed by semantic_interpretation.py:770-773 for all three renderings — :779 build_prompt, :810 retry_prompt, :950 the answer tool). CLOSED by `own_uks` (semantic_store.ML:804-808): this run's own keys never enter `wanted_uks`, so never `available` (:809-822), so `sem_of` returns NONE. Verified that `own_uks` really is the whole run: `build_entries`'s only non-test caller is `enumerate_entries` (:1739), handed the post-dedup `all_entries_with_pos`; `build_entries` only maps over `raw`; the wire `entries'` is a 1:1 map (:1800-1825), so `own_uks` == `AgentTask.theory_keys` (semantic_interpretation.py:475).

PATH 2 — batch prompt, the entry line itself: `_label(e)` + `e.prop_str` + line number (semantic_interpretation.py:766-769). CANNOT DISCLOSE. `mk_prop_str` (semantic_store.ML:695-729) prints the proposition or type, and for Type / Class / Locale / Theorem_Collection / Method the Isabelle SOURCE of the declaring command — never stored English.
PATH 3 — batch prompt, theorem-collection member preview (`mk_prompt_hint`, semantic_store.ML:733-753). CANNOT DISCLOSE: up to ten member propositions via `pp (Thm.prop_of thm)`.

PATH 4 — batch prompt, the hint's other lines: `Template <id>: <prop>` (semantic_store.ML:882-885) and `Under this instantiation the same proposition also arises from: …` (:889-893). CANNOT DISCLOSE: a printed proposition and template NAMES; neither goes through `sem_of`. (This is why §15.8's word 'only' is wrong — see rest-plan-hint-collapsed.)

PATH 5 — `query` tool, name lookup: `query_by_name_raw` -> `Semantic_DB.query` (semantics.py:1656). CLOSED by `hidden_keys` on the RESOLVED key (semantics.py:1783-1785): the text is fetched and then discarded, `refused(typed)` is returned instead.
PATH 6 — `query` tool, short-name fallback (semantics.py:1795-1798). CLOSED by `hidden_keys` on the resolved key, same shape.

PATH 7 — `query` tool, notation fallback `_try_resolve_syntax_token` (semantics.py:1713-1721). CLOSED by `hidden_keys`, and here the store is not even consulted (`sem = None if uk in hidden_keys else Semantic_DB.query(...)`, :1714). My probe over the shipped function records 0 `Semantic_DB.query` calls on the hidden branch.

PATH 8 — `query` tool, `show_defs` -> `_append_definition` -> `_get_definition_source` (semantics.py:1663-1676). CANNOT DISCLOSE: it returns the source of the defining Isabelle command, which is exactly what D18 tells the agent to read. NOTE, not a leak: since the round-two rearrangement the hidden NOTATION branch also reaches it (probe: `append called: 1`), unlike the tool's other two refusals, which return first — the divergence is ordered fixed under rest-rearrange-showdefs.

PATH 9 — `query` tool, the `LookupError` text for an entity with no interpretation (semantics.py:1657-1660, returned at :1789). CANNOT DISCLOSE: no stored text; it reveals only the boolean 'has / has not been interpreted'.

PATH 10 — `desugar_and_explain` tool, per-constant annotation (desugar.py:131). CLOSED by `hidden_keys` (desugar.py:126-129), checked before the `Semantic_DB.query` AND before `seen_constants.add`, so a hidden constant is neither described nor marked as told.

PATH 11 — `definition` tool (hover.py:222). CANNOT DISCLOSE: it answers from `pide_state.command_at_position`; hover.py imports no Semantic_DB at all (verified by reading its import block, hover.py:8-15).
PATH 12 — `hover` tool (hover.py:286-339). CANNOT DISCLOSE: Isabelle's own PIDE tooltip.

PATH 13 — the ML callbacks the interpretation session registers (`interpret_file_callbacks`, semantic_store.ML:1836-1856: universal_key, theory long-name/path, desugar, resolve_notation, the config lookup and the eleven entity enumerators). CANNOT DISCLOSE. `query_semantics_by_key` (:341-349) is the only ML reader of stored English in either repository; its callers are `query_semantics` (:350, whose only caller is Test/Test_All.thy:166) and `sem_of` (:856). Tools/explain_term.ML and Isabelle_RPC/Tools/context.ML contain no store read (greps for `Semantic_DB` / `query_semantics` / `Semantic_Store.` return only comments).

PATH 14 — `task.results[i] = results[i]` for not-enrolled entries (semantic_interpretation.py:1824), the one place this theory's stored English lives inside the task. CANNOT DISCLOSE: every reader of `results[` (:519 enqueue nulls it, :731 on_answer, :847 the judge's `why`, :1440 and :1456 the gate, :1896 the missing count, :1913 the return to Isabelle) is the queue, the gate or the result, never a prompt or a tool reply; and the answer tool refuses any index whose state is `_NOT_ENROLLED` (:920-922), so a prefilled slot can never become a gate's `fresh`.

PATH 15 — `InterpretationResult.interpretations` / `pretty_prints` (semantic_interpretation.py:1913 and :276-280). CANNOT DISCLOSE to the agent: they travel back to Isabelle, never into the agent's conversation.
PATH 16 — `_report` progress lines (semantic_interpretation.py:1000-1013, called from the answer tool at :940). CANNOT DISCLOSE: `Connection.writeln` into Isabelle, carrying counts and theory names.

PATH 17 — the prefilter's two embedding documents (`_prefilter`, semantic_interpretation.py:1303-1308). These DO carry the baseline text, but they go to the embedding SERVICE, not into any agent conversation; no interpretation-session channel touches them. Outside D18's scope by construction.

PATH 18 — the judge session's prompt (`JudgeTask.build_prompt`, semantic_interpretation.py:838-843) carries `rec.baseline_interpretation` BY DESIGN (D12, §5.4 step 3). Confirmed it cannot reach the interpretation session: the judge driver is built with `tools=[mk_verdict_tool(judge)]` and `cli_tools=False` (:1800-1808), `JudgeTask.format_entries` renders labels only (:836-837) and its `retry_prompt` is a fixed string (:853-856).

PATH 19 — the out-of-process (Codex) backend. CLOSED identically: `build_mcp_server` serves the SAME tool objects the in-process path built (codex.py:229 passes `self.tools`), so the `hidden_keys` closure is the same one.

PATH 20 — OPEN, out of band: the CLI built-ins. The interpretation session is built without a `cli_tools` argument (semantic_interpretation.py:1848-1856) and the default is True (interpretation_driver/__init__.py:118), so the permission hook's allow-set is the five MCP tools plus `_CLI_BUILTINS` — Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Bash, Skill, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch, the task tools (claude_code.py:67-86, :428-429). The store is a plain on-disk LMDB and its reader is an importable package, so an agent that chose to look could read what D18 hides. Deliberately left open: D18 instructs the agent to read the theory source, which is what Read/Grep/Glob are for, and no prompt or tool text names the store, its path or its API. D18's own wording ('nothing HANDS the agent a stored interpretation') is a statement about what the pipeline provides and remains accurate.
